title: fix(workers): required worker sessions fail during workspace binding
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes HTTP 500 when a required-worker session prepares its workspace while retaining a canonical session reader.

## User Impact

Required native workers can bind a new session workspace without invalidating their admitted session read. No configuration, schema, permission, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opaque commit callback selects a native transaction on the same handle retained by dispatch admission. Its canonical-reader check rejects that active transaction with `Canonical session reader continuation is no longer current` before the first model request can run.

Source-free workspace bindings now use the existing worker-write grant contract, which validates host authority at planning and commit boundaries without opening a transaction on the retained reader. Inherited workspace source callbacks keep their native atomicity because they may read other stores. The strict reader-currency and revocation checks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression exercises the actual canonical-reader admission and workspace committer. Before the fix: 1 failed, 2 passed, with the exact live error. After: 3 passed. Changed Gateway file: 25.48 seconds including cold worker compilation, 4.251 seconds of test execution; CI seconds not yet measured.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-worker-placement-dispatch-admission.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-entry-patch.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-canonical-reader-continuation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 47 passed, 0 failed; 50.12 seconds including cold worker compilation. Includes post-planning/final-grant revocation, canonical continuation replacement, and unsettled-custody controls.
- Required authoring-cost command on the publication head: `pnpm test src/gateway/server-worker-placement-dispatch-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed, wall time 19.47 seconds, Vitest duration 16.55 seconds; the new regression took 1.240 seconds. Hosted CI seconds are unmeasured (draft CI is skipped).
- Exact publication head `1a2be292f52b725977b421509686675fff2e96e5`: the same 47 focused tests passed with zero failures/skips in 62.19 seconds; scoped oxlint, formatting and diff checks passed. Affected owner and regression bytes match the reviewed image repair.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, no actionable findings.
- Changed-file guards, formatting, core production typecheck, and all 27 core test type graphs passed. Broad dead-export scan remains red on unchanged base UI exports: `sessionPlacementRecoveryScopeStoragePrefix` and exports of `session-placement-recovery.v2026-9-8.test-support.ts`. This is not an all-gates-green claim; no scanner bypass or unrelated UI edits.
- Canonical Linux ARM64 Docker build, exact packaged revision, network-disabled native configuration validation, and owned-node containerd/CRI immutable digest verification passed.

**Full authenticated native OpenShell E2E passed**: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped/cancelled; test 254.766 seconds, overall Node run 255.316 seconds. The selected branch is `openclaw` in the existing real OpenShell integration, not the separate Codex-specific tool/network/withdrawal branch.

Exact inputs: OCE `684b6b64882b817ab5e81e8829bb44d22e964a53` (clean committed checkout), OpenClaw runtime source `edf98f2b251e88175e3e90b49fea484c190c2704`, immutable Linux ARM64 manifest `sha256:006bdb505463ee41f6604abc1e9ce9a7fb6a3f274bc67d81e54a3c18253da33e`. OCI revision and packaged build-info match the source; network-disabled schema validation and owned-node containerd/CRI digest checks passed before model execution. Native fixture SHA-256: `88784800e402e11a049f6dfaae9f820cd3a86f98231bc0dd0b85f3450deb3eec`.

| Real boundary | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Provider startup/private temporary initialization and model probe | Passed |
| Native node enrollment, including Gateway replacement | Passed |
| Provider-owned mount identity and credential separation | Passed |
| Real workspace API PUT/GET | Passed |
| First Gateway model session through a native worker | Passed, HTTP 200 |
| Second successive session with the first worker retained | Passed, HTTP 200 |
| Embedded mode refused before provisioning | Passed |

The earlier first-session HTTP 500 was reproduced by a core regression and repaired through existing worker-write grants in [OpenClaw #167162](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167162), preserving canonical-reader currency and revocation checks. Once repaired, the first model session passed but Kubernetes OOM-killed the native workload during the second session at the fixture's 2Gi container limit. The native-only fixture now aligns Compute/Sandbox budgets at 6Gi and supplies a 16Gi namespace quota. Capacity 2 and retained-worker behavior remain unchanged; these are bounded fixture budgets, not a measured production minimum. Codex defaults are unchanged.

The existing approved credential was loaded privately through 1Password CLI and reused through a task-owned tmux launcher. No credential bytes entered builds, source or recorded output; the separate Gateway remains credential-free. The isolated database was removed and all task-owned namespaces verified absent, preserving baseline resources.

The full E2E image uses the reviewed EDF repair on the previously tested candidate, not the mechanically rebased publication head `1a2be292f52b725977b421509686675fff2e96e5`. Affected producer, admission, canonical guard, patch/writer and regression bytes match; 47 scoped tests and lint/format checks passed again on the exact publication head. This is not an exact-publication-head full-image claim. The PR remains draft; no merge, release or registry publication.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/1698 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/1708.
